scope: Canonical dashboard review; official-source research; no private records; no attorney review

findings.finding: Yes for covered tenant-occupied units: Housing Inventory reporting generates the Rent Increase License. No individual-owner exemption and no separate per-increase approval application. Current license is required on the effective date; completing reporting before notice is recommended.

The Treasurer exception applies only by reason of rental income from one structure with fewer than four units (or specified condo/co-op facts); other business activity can trigger registration. Two supplied units do not establish the total building unit count.
$3,995.00 × 1.6% = $63.92; $3,995.00 + $63.92 = $4,058.92. Conditional on verified base, lease authority, license, coverage and timing.

Assuming no intervening increase and an eligible February 1, 2027 event, skipped 1.4% plus current 1.6% is 3.0% = $119.85; new rent $4,114.85. Both banking measuring points are satisfied on that assumed history.
$3,150.00 is supplied as June 1, 2019 lease-start rent, not certified current base. Annual-only illustration is $50.40 to $3,200.40.
Only if the base remains $3,150.00 and no increases intervened: 11.5% banked plus 1.6% current = 13.1% = $412.65; new rent $3,562.65. Not a certified maximum.

Civil Code §827 requires 30 days for increases of 10% or less and 90 days above 10%; California mail adds five calendar days under CCP §1013. The Board multiple-year page’s 30/35-day shorthand must not override the statute.
Official state guidance says rent cannot be raised during a fixed term unless the agreement expressly allows it. Unit 1’s April 2026 instrument is missing.

Rule 13.14 makes an annual/banked increase effective while unlicensed entirely null and void; filing restores future authority prospectively and does not retroactively validate the void increase. Otherwise lawful banking rights are preserved.
Section 37.3(b)(5) has a null-and-void rule, but Rules 4.10(b) and 4.12(b) contain text-specific exceptions. Include full annual/banked itemization and dates rather than relying on an exception.

No property-specific dollar amount is established. Actual tenancy commencement, net taxable value, total units and applicable tax bills are missing. Official 2026–27 factors are 0.0044 for FY2018–19 and 0.0041 for FY2024–25 only if those are the actual commencement years.
The 2026–27 bond worksheet says small-building licensing applies to increases effective on or after March 1, 2022; Rule 13.14 and §37.15 say March 1, 2023. Use the ordinance/rule and flag the form.

The Board convenience text lists Ordinance 3-26 effective February 9, 2026; the official publisher history lists February 8, 2026. This does not change the 2026–27 annual rate, but the discrepancy is published rather than silently resolved.

Raising one unit is not automatically discrimination; protected-class or arbitrary personal-characteristic selection, retaliation and bad-faith pressure remain unlawful. Identical increases are not immunity.
No official dataset establishes typical SF corporate versus individual increase behavior. The DOJ RealPage release is a proposed-settlement enforcement example, not a universal practice statistic.

No actual attorney review occurred. The dashboard provides a simulated tenant-side checklist, official petition routes, and explicit evidence gaps. Rent-history/unlawful-rent petitions have no filing time limit; qualifying repair petitions have a 60-day deadline.

The verified routine local planning reference is the 1.6% annual allowance. No official ZIP-specific market-normal percentage was located; legal permissibility is not a market average or guarantee of acceptance.

The website uses placeholders and preserves supplied dates/amounts. Official Housing Inventory submissions require truthful owner/business contact information and are public; placeholders must not be submitted to the City.
The preserved review/ generator used the current date, causing generated output to drift from committed pages. Integration must pin its generation date and add a drift gate.

findings.item: Pending banked-increase cap is not law
findings.finding: Legistar File #261020 was independently re-fetched on 2026-11-08: Pending Committee Action, no final action, no enactment date. The proposed 10% cap is not applied to current arithmetic; re-check before any large catch-up.
